description: Two source instances of the same Clearing Member functional role flank the CCP; both dashed associations are bidirectional. The artwork does not identify a particular institution or distinguish these instances as buyer and seller. T10 defines the functional participants and T11 maps business roles to them. General and individual clearing memberships remain distinct contextual cases within the canonical definition.

The seven outward arrows from Clearing identify high-level scope relationships, not temporal message exchanges or UML include/extend semantics. Risk Management contains Netting and Margining plus Default Fund Contribution; Settlement Management contains Settlement (Netting) and Buy in; Reporting contains Cash and Fails. Reporting and Collateral Management are shaded out-of-scope context. P109 expressly says the diagram is non-exhaustive and shows those two processes only for completeness.

Two separate source start points represent the accepted-trade and cancellation paths. The negative cancellation decision ends immediately; the positive branch cancels the trade leg and the member processes the cancellation. Pink trading-venue notes provide out-of-scope trigger context, not additional message arrows. T12 preserves the independent trade-matching cases, contact with a trading member firm, and the opposite-trade alternative. Start/End words are explanatory marker labels added to the source circles.

The end-of-real-time-session milestone leads to position netting by the CCP and information processing by the clearing member. T13 additionally describes a business-session status message, house/client margin-account netting, reconciliation using netting parameters, and possible intraday margin on provisional net positions. The milestone box is source context, not an ISO message name.

The source start branches to risk calculation/information and margin-call follow-up. Scenario 1 permits automatic cash debit; Scenario 2 allows the member to propose collateral. CCP rejection leads to the member choosing whether to propose again; acceptance reaches a parallel bar, followed by receiving and delivering securities/cash. The three out-of-scope cash/securities paths share the source end marker. The source bar is retained as a thick bar symbol, not converted into an exclusive decision. T14 supplies collateral-deficit conditions and the CCP-rule dependency.

The CCP assesses risk and calculates the contribution, while the member processes the result. A sufficient contribution reaches the source end marker; a deficit enters an out-of-scope payment process. The source does not draw an end beyond the payment process, so none is added. T15 preserves daily/monthly calculation, automatic debit or payment on behalf under power of attorney, optional margin calls, and possible return of excess.

Three source lanes assign CSD reporting/processing, CCP updates/netting/event application/instruction building, and clearing-member information processing. The three CCP optional activities remain individually labeled; CNS-only applies to position/instruction update. Both CSD event input and settlement results are preserved, as are all three final paths. T16 additionally describes clearing-member instructions to a paying agent, the power-of-attorney exception, and failed-trade reporting when the general clearing member is absent from the settlement chain.

The warning starts X days after intended settlement date. A clearing member may request delay; the CCP acknowledges and that response path ends. The source also has a thin curved warning-to-launch connector annotated And/or; it is preserved as a directed And/or relationship without imposing an exclusive decision. Launch notification reaches a source parallel bar feeding CCP settlement-instruction cancellation and later buy-in confirmation. Confirmation is annotated Buy in Date +1 and leads to out-of-scope payment and member cancellation of its settlement-agent instruction. T17 says acknowledgment is by telephone, delay is valid only for continuous netting systems, and confirmation is one business day after buy-in. Source labels are retained; no fixed number of days is invented.
